newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia growth seen up in 1997/98 budget - paper.
newsitem.headline: Australia growth seen up in 1997/98 budget - paper.

text.p: The Australian government will forecast an economic growth rate of 3.5 percent to 3.75 percent for the 1997/98 financial year when the budget is handed down on Tuesday, according to a newspaper report published on Monday.
The Australian newspaper also reported the government would forecast employment growth of well over two percent and an unemployment rate of around eight percent by June 1998.
April figures showed unemployment at 8.7 percent, with employment rising by 37,100.
In its most recent forecasts, made in January, the government predicted economic growth of 3.5 percent in 1997/98 and employment growth of two percent.
Both The Australian and The Sydney Morning Herald said health would take the brunt of the expected A$2.0 billion in government spending cuts, although childcare assistance was also likely to suffer.

The Sydney Morning Herald said the budget would contain a new tax rebate aimed at low and middle income earners, which would reduce the amount of tax paid on interest earned on bank accounts and other investments.
The new tax rebate on savings would be paid for by the A$4.5 billion set aside by the former Labor government to provide a subsidy for superannuation savings.
"The savings incentive ... will be the big selling point in the budget," the newspaper said.
"(It) will give major benefits to retirees and others who depend on savings income."

The Age newspaper reported that aged Australians would also benefit from a special budget package which would award them retirement bonuses worth thousands of dollars if they deferred pension entitlements for up to five years.

On the business side, The Australian Financial Review reported that industry assistance schemes would not be cut in the 1997/98 budget, and the 125 percent research and development programme would be maintained.
A new capped tax rebate scheme would be introduced to replace the abolished infrastructure bond programme, the newspaper said.
Treasurer Peter Costello will hand down the budget at 7.30 p.m. (0930 GMT) on Tuesday.
